nodes.title: How to Use
widgets_values:
The workflow processing reads from left to right: get details about the image and create a mask, select which parameters to enable (muters), set the saved image parameters, run the optional stages.

### How to use: 

At first run, disable (Mute) all Stages.

Load an image (PNG recommended) and click `Run`.

You will be shown most of the generation parameters used (if embedded within the image, otherwise in the notes, you will see something similar to "ERROR: No generation metadata found. Using the SDXL bottle starter preset; these settings were not extracted from the image.").  You will not be shown the model type (Anima, ...), so you will have to find that information. What you will also see is if LoraManager has a local copy of the model or its LoRAs. If it does, use the model selection and fill (you can link most of the inputs to the corresponding "LC Show Any" nodes). Those values are used to store as metadata within the saved image for easier classification. Note: You do not have to use the original model type to run any of the stages in the workflow, they are all `img2img` based.

Select which stage you want to enable:
- Stage 1: `Rescale to X MP` allows images to be rescale to a target MegaPixels value. Keep in mind that the larger the image, the longer it might take to process with added VRAM usage. 4MP is a good mid-point, given you can use a final upscaler stage.
- Stage 2: `Model Resampler` has two optional mode: "Initial" (S2a) for a simple resampling using the selected model and "Extra" (S2b) for a more detailed rendering. Not all models will benefit from this step.
- Stage 3: `Inpainting Detailers` requires you to manually add a mask on the input image (right click on the image and select "Open in Mask Editor...") and add content to be redrawn (ex: add a finger), then have the tool find the element specified (see a to d, only 1x can be used for a single run) to be redrawn.
- Stage 4: `SAM Detailers` uses SAM 3.1 to find the element specified (see a to d, only 1x can be used for a single run). This method uses the `small` detection, for example a small face take less than 1/16 of the area of the image and will apply a larger denoise to it.
- Stage 5: Final Upscaler` uses VOSR2 to 2.0x the width and the height of the image (ie if the source image is 4MP, it will be 4 *2 *2 = 16MP after the upscale)


Hit `Run` and decide if you like the result or want to try again with different parameters.

Use the saved image as the input to the next run to fix another component if desired.

ComfyUI Manager: some nodes might not be resolved by default and might need to be installed from git directly.
1. https://github.com/lonecatone23/ComfyUI_LC123_nodes
2. https://github.com/lonecatone23/ComfyUI_LC_MaskMaker_nodes

VRAM Control **attempts**
widgets_values:
Those bypassers serve as an extra option to attempt to release VRAM (using ComfyUI with an attention CLI parameter is recommended). Note that "yes" means "allow the node to run".
- `Clean VRAM` will **attempt** to release content from the VRAM. This is in addition to how ComfyUI performs its own caching.
- `VRAM Debug` will display the amount of VRAM available to be used. It will also **attempt** to release some as possible. The `Unload all models` below is another toggle available to **attempt** to free additional VRAM.

nodes.title: Inpainting
widgets_values:
ℹ️ In the image loader make sure to create a mask that cover the area to fix/inpaint.
ℹ️ If you are going to fix via inpainting, and need to "add a finger", make sure to paint the missing one before asking for the stage to run.
ℹ️ Only one of a to d can be enabled at a time.
ℹ️ a is "custom", ie enter your own text.
ℹ️ use the `denoise` to replace more ( increase) or less (decrease).
ℹ️ the `SEGSPreview` should show you the mask you drew, confirming it is applying the requested change to that area alone.
